**Sentence 1: Row space and nullspace**

The row space of a matrix A is the set of all linear combinations of the rows of A. The nullspace of A is the set of all vectors x such that Ax = 0.

The statement claims that the row space of A is orthogonal to the nullspace. This means that if you take any vector x in the nullspace and project it onto any row of A, the result will be the zero vector.

To see why this is true, consider the equation Ax = 0. This equation says that the dot product of x with each row of A is 0. In other words, if you take the dot product of x with the i-th row of A, denoted as r_i, you get 0.

(a_1r_1 + a_2r_2 +... + a_nr_n) · x = a_1(r_1 · x) + a_2(r_2 · x) +... + a_n(r_n · x)

Since r_i · x = 0 for each i, we have:

(a_1r_1 + a_2r_2 +... + a_nr_n) · x = a_1(0) + a_2(0) +... + a_n(0) = 0

This shows that the dot product of any vector in the row space of A with any vector in the nullspace is 0. Therefore, the row space of A is orthogonal to the nullspace.
